items.title: Arsenal outclassed in defeat to dominant Lyon
items.excerpt: Arsenal’s hopes of automatic qualification to the Women’s Champions League quarter-finals are hanging by a thread after they were beaten 2-0 at home by a dominant Lyon in foggy conditions.
body: Arsenal’s hopes of automatic qualification to the Women’s Champions League quarter-finals are hanging by a thread after they were beaten 2-0 at home by a dominant Lyon in foggy conditions.

The French side, who beat Arsenal in the semi-finals last season, got the better of the Gunners again at Meadow Park on Thursday night with goals from Jule Brand and Melchie Dumornay in each half sealing the victory.

Arsenal barely laid a glove on Lyon - who are yet to concede a goal in this season's Champions League - and now sit eighth in the standings, three points adrift of fourth-placed Chelsea, after their first loss in five league phase matches. items.title: England handed suspended away ticket ban for fans' chants in Spain
items.excerpt: England have been given a suspended away ticket ban by UEFA for "racist and/or discriminatory behaviour" by their fans during the 3-2 win over Spain in Madrid.
body: England have been given a suspended away ticket ban by UEFA for "racist and/or discriminatory behaviour" by their fans during the 3-2 win over Spain in Madrid.
The punishment is a one-match ban and is suspended for a "probationary period" of two years.
Sky Sports News understands the punishment is for anti-Catholic and anti-Irish chanting during the Nations League match.

A spokesperson for The FA told Sky Sports News : " We will not tolerate this unacceptable and deeply offensive chanting, and will work with the police who attend all England home and away matches to identify the perpetrators and take the necessary action."

items.title: Seven years on from the sack at Spurs what sort of coach is Pochettino now?
items.excerpt: What Mauricio Pochettino achieved with Tottenham Hotspur in the previous decade looks even more impressive now than it did at the time. Manchester United really should have turned to the popular Argentine coach years ago.
body: What Mauricio Pochettino achieved with Tottenham Hotspur in the previous decade looks even more impressive now than it did at the time. Manchester United really should have turned to the popular Argentine coach years ago.

In his five full seasons in charge, Spurs were in the Premier League's top five each time - a run that has never been bettered in their history. He took the club above Arsenal for the first time in a generation and into a Champions League final for the first time ever.

Silverware was missing, much to the amusement of his critics, but the charges against Manchester City serve as a reminder that he was playing with the deck stacked against him. He overachieved and it is his thrilling football that endures in the memory.

items.title: Man City have problems - is Fernandez their most obvious?
items.excerpt: Enzo Maresca is being forced to work within an unprecedented set of circumstances this season. Up until recently, his fixation on football matters served to quieten the noise around the club. But now the anomalous nature of Manchester City'…
body: Enzo Maresca is being forced to work within an unprecedented set of circumstances this season. Up until recently, his fixation on football matters served to quieten the noise around the club. But now the anomalous nature of Manchester City's situation is apparent on and off the pitch.

Maresca began with seven straight wins in all competitions. He has since suffered a hat-trick of Premier League defeats. Concerns over performance levels in certain phases existed from the start but have come into sharper focus as results have nosedived.

Stylistically, City are far too open; just as easy to play through as play over. Only Newcastle (20) have faced more shots from fast breaks since the start of term than City's 17, conceding two goals from such situations in defeat to Nottingham Forest before the international break. body: The Premier League is back after the recent international break and the Sky Sports football writers dissect all the major talking points ahead of another busy weekend's action. Man City vs Fulham: Cottagers ideal opponents to get City back to winning ways
Are Man City in crisis heading into Saturday lunchtime's clash against Fulham, with Enzo Maresca's side having lost their previous three Premier League contests to lose top spot to Arsenal?
Those trio of reverses against Aston Villa, Brighton and, just prior to the international break, Nottingham Forest, mean City have now lost as many times as in their previous 36 league outings.

Since the start of 2007-08, though, City have only been beaten in four successive top-flight games on two occasions, in August 2008 and December 2024, and it would take a massive leap of faith to suggest Fulham are the team to inflict such ignominy on them this weekend.
